clue.text: Monster herb is leek in the end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept from the vegetable

blocks.note: a common kitchen herb
taken as written
final letter of leek

explanation.surface: A gardener's oddity: a herb that is somehow a leek at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilisk is a mythical reptile whose gaze could kill, a legendary beast of medieval bestiaries.

clue.text: Top fellow to chill with

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
to ice is to chill

explanation.surface: The top bloke to relax and hang out with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the upper part of a dress or a close-fitting garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Problem solver when things heat up

blocks.note: first meaning: one who sums, doing arithmetic problems
second meaning: the hot season of the year

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a troubleshooter brought in when tensions rise; the first sense is a jokey word for someone doing sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer is the warmest season, and read as sum-mer it names a person who adds figures to solve problems.

clue.text: Ferris wheel marathon nearly finished you

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the word for a marathon is cut short at the end

blocks.note: a marathon session is a long one
done means finished
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A tired runner is told the marathon is nearly over at the big wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marathon' tempts towards the London Marathon, but it only means long here.
explanation.definitionFit: The London Eye is the giant observation wheel on the Thames South Bank, a large Ferris wheel.

clue.text: Geordie singer claims accent hurt work in rock

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the singer's name wraps round the other words

blocks.note: Sting, the singer, comes from Newcastle; a Geordie is a native of Tyneside
tone of voice, an accent
a cut is a hurt

explanation.surface: A rock star from Newcastle hurt his accent working in rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert goes in after the first letter of the singer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecutting is the craft of shaping stone, literal work in rock, while the surface suggests rock music.

clue.text: Pensioner, possibly one banging on?

blocks.note: first meaning: a baby ..., born after the war and now often retired
second meaning: something that booms, making a loud noise

explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibes at older people who bang on about things; the second reading is literal, one who booms.
explanation.definitionFit: Boomer is slang for the post-war generation, many now drawing pensions, and also literally a thing that makes a deep resounding noise.

clue.text: Stars lit up drinking port

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the lit-up word takes the port inside it

blocks.note: a light that is lit is on
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Celebrities get drunk on port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' and 'drinking' suggest getting drunk; port is the city, not the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Orion is a prominent constellation, a group of stars named for the hunter of Greek myth.

clue.text: Police force completely in charge of copper?

blocks.note: the Met, London's Metropolitan Police
all means completely
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A question of whether the whole police force is under one officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper is slang for a police officer, but here it is the metal; the question mark flags copper as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a metal, so something made of copper is metallic in nature.

clue.text: Local piano exported from Cleveland?

indicators.note: something exported is sent out, so the letter leaves the word

blocks.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Grover Cleveland was twice a US president

explanation.surface: A local piano being shipped out of the Cleveland area.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleveland looks like the place; it is the person, Grover Cleveland, so the question mark marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is someone who lives in the area, so a resident of the place.

clue.text: Power to impersonate cartoon henchman

blocks.note: to do someone is to mimic them
the yellow henchmen of the Despicable Me films

explanation.surface: An impressionist hopes to gain power by doing a cartoon sidekick.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereign authority or control over territory and people, so it is a synonym for rule.

clue.text: Knock about answer with puzzlers on break

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the striking word goes round the single letter
in a down-free across reading, on means attached after, so the pronoun follows

blocks.note: to knock is to strike
A is the usual abbreviation for answer
the setter and solvers, the people puzzling

explanation.surface: Puzzle-solvers knock an answer about while on their tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or gap in a sequence, a synonym for an interruption or rest.

clue.text: Graze pasty, shocked that is Cornish fare

indicators.note: something shocked is jolted out of its normal state, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone nibbling a pasty is shocked to hear it counts as Cornish food.
explanation.walkthrough: The pasty is itself Cornish fare, which tempts you to take it as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stargazey pie is a traditional dish from Cornwall, baked with pilchard heads poking up through the pastry.

clue.text: I believe workers mostly party

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for workers loses its last letter

blocks.note: a crew is a team of workers
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A statement of faith that most workers like a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Credo is Latin for 'I believe', the opening word of the Creed, and so names a statement of belief.

clue.text: Caught folk rockers hiding leader and daughter

indicators.note: hiding the leader means the band's first letter is concealed, so it is dropped

blocks.note: Pentangle was a British folk-rock band of the late 1960s
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Members of a folk band are caught hiding their frontman and his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: You need to know the band Pentangle; 'folk rockers' is not a general word for musicians here.
explanation.definitionFit: Entangled means trapped or snared in something like a net, so it works as a synonym for caught.

clue.text: Wild intercourse keeps Romeo coming back

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so the act takes in the letter
wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A racy note: passionate sex keeps the lover Romeo coming back for more.
explanation.walkthrough: The R can go anywhere inside, since the whole lot is then mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurrection is rising from the dead, a return to life, which is a coming back.

clue.text: Drink money docked to pay for university

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is, so the following phrase loses its final letter

blocks.note: coin is money
to treat someone is to pay for them
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student's money is docked to pay university fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, a branded alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Fit social worker bored by old hairdo

indicators.note: a thing bored by another is drilled into, so the next letter goes inside the word for fit

blocks.note: buff means physically fit and muscular
O is the abbreviation for old
ants are social insects and workers

explanation.surface: An attractive social worker is bored by an old-fashioned hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: The grammar suggests 'fit social worker' is one person; fit is separate and the old letter bores into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouffant is a puffed-out, backcombed hairstyle, so a type of hairdo.

clue.text: Avoid getting up, following school calendar

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top
following means placed after, so the school abbreviation comes first

blocks.note: SCH is an abbreviation for school
to elude is to avoid

explanation.surface: Skipping the early morning start to keep pace with the school timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a timetable or list of planned events, as a calendar is.

clue.text: Start to conduct others, snarling "hit it" here?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept from conduct
snarling suggests tangled up, so the letters are knotted into a new order

blocks.note: first letter of conduct
taken as written
to rap is to strike
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conductor starts the band by growling 'hit it' at the players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here?' points at the place the scene happens: the sunken area where musicians play for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the area below the stage where the band plays, the very place a conductor would cue them in.

clue.text: Small insect bit

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a midge is a tiny biting fly

explanation.surface: A tiny insect has bitten someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as the past of bite; it is the noun meaning a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidge is a tiny amount, informal for a smidgen, meaning a little bit.

clue.text: Sorry fellow, below standard

indicators.note: below means underneath in a down entry, so the fellow sits after the standard

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A pitiful man whose work falls below the expected standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry fellow' looks like one phrase; the definition is only the interjection asking someone to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections used to ask someone to repeat what they said, or to apologise.

clue.text: Independent swimmer cracks far side of the Channel

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so the fish goes inside the country

blocks.note: the country across the English Channel from Britain
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: A lone swimmer attempts to make it across the English Channel to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' looks like a nod to the newspaper, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance is self-employed, working for various clients rather than one employer, so is independent.

clue.text: Passed on eating last of duck pancake

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept from duck
eating means taking in, so the word for passed on swallows the letter

blocks.note: the late someone has died, passed on
final letter of duck

explanation.surface: Someone declined a pancake while eating duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed on' looks like declining food; it means died.
explanation.definitionFit: A latke is a Jewish potato pancake, traditionally fried and eaten at Hanukkah.

clue.text: You shouldn't have elected politician with a Florida resort

blocks.note: said when thanking for a gift, and ta is British slang for thanks
a Member of Parliament is elected
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a gift of a Florida holiday from their MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida, popular with holidaymakers, so fits as a resort there.

clue.text: A place like Cambridge maintains universal sharpness

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the place holds the letter within it

blocks.note: taken as written
Cambridge has city status, one example of such a place
U is the film-rating letter for universal

explanation.surface: A university town boasts of keeping its universal intellectual edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuity means keenness of thought or vision, a synonym for mental sharpness.

clue.text: Brilliant child loses head after second place finish

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for child gives up its first letter
after places the beheaded child behind the preceding pieces

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for place
an end is a finish
a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A gifted child sulks after only finishing in second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid means magnificent or excellent, a close synonym for brilliant as praise.

clue.text: Match official's card shown in rows

blocks.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
the red card a referee shows to send a player off

explanation.surface: A referee's card is held up in front of rows of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match official' reads as one unit, the referee, but it splits: Match is one piece and official's card another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered describes things set in rising layers or banks, as seating arranged one row above another.

clue.text: Ecru? Dreadfully thin colour

indicators.note: something done dreadfully is done badly, so these letters are messed up

blocks.note: taken as written
lean means thin

explanation.surface: A decorator dismisses a pale beige shade as dreadfully thin.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecru is itself a colour, so it looks like the definition, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky blue, a named shade like ecru.
